# 08.0 Your HTML Journey Continues

Congratulations — you've built a real foundation. You can now structure a page from scratch with valid, semantic, accessible HTML: the skeleton and the DOM, headings and text, links and navigation, images and media, semantic structure, clean markup, and even working alongside AI to generate it responsibly.

![GENERATING: Conceptual illustration of web development layers: HTML as the structural foundation layer at the bottom, CSS as the styling layer in the middle, and JavaScript as the interactive behavior layer on top, shown as a layered cake with clear labels and color coding to differentiate each technology](/.learn/assets/jbagejzsqqc)

## What Comes Next

HTML is the structural layer of every web page — the layers above it build on the meaning you've learned to express:

- **CSS** styles that structure: colors, layout, typography, and responsive design.
- **JavaScript** adds behavior: interactivity, animation, and dynamic content.
- **Projects** are where it all sticks — build a personal site, a portfolio, or a small multi-page project and apply what you know end to end.

The most useful next step is to keep writing HTML by hand. Pick a page you admire, inspect its structure in developer tools, and try to recreate it semantically — then run it through the W3C validator to confirm it's clean.

To go further, these references are worth bookmarking:

- [MDN Web Docs: HTML Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML)
- [W3C HTML Validator](https://validator.w3.org/)
- [WebAIM: Web Accessibility](https://webaim.org/)
- [Can I Use: Browser Support](https://caniuse.com/)

Every web developer started exactly where you are now, and the structure you've mastered is the part that everything else depends on.
